chunks: Are they better than the people of Tubba, and those who had lived before them, whom We destroyed as they were sinners?

key_terms.قَوْمُ تُبَّعٍ: The people of Tubba (a title for South Arabian kings)

ai.seo_question: Who were the people of Tubba and why were they destroyed according to the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse serves as a stern warning to the Quraysh by invoking the fate of Tubba', a Himyarite king whose destruction is often cited as a precedent for divine retribution against arrogant polytheists. The rhetorical comparison underscores the continuity of God's justice, suggesting that just as previous nations were annihilated for their sins, the Meccans face imminent ruin unless they embrace the truth. This highlights the practical implication of repentance as the only means to avert the same historical pattern of destruction.
